title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)' notes axiomatise 'ateliers' (workshops). An atelier is a structured category or poset F of 'figures', meaning combinatorial or tame-topological cells. Inside it sit a class L of minimal ('linear', point-like) figures and a class M of distinguished figures. These carry a relation x ≪ F ('x is a point/vertex of F'), an interior version x ∘≪ F, and voisb(F), the set of points of L lying in F. The axioms are numbered At 1–At 14 bis. On p. 91 he starts studying a sub-atelier F' ⊂ F. At 1–7 transfer at once to F'. The axioms involving L (At 8, 9, 9_Σ, 10) require comparing the minimal elements L' of F' with L ∩ F'. One always has L ∩ F' ⊂ L'.

This page opens by asking for equality: every element of F' that is minimal for ≪ in F' should already be minimal in F. To secure this he introduces two conditions on a sub-atelier.
(i) 'Épais' (thick, saturated for points), condition Sous-at 3: if X ∈ M' = F' ∩ M and x ∈ L with x ≪ X, then x ∈ F'. Equivalently voisb(X) ⊂ F'. This is a downward-closure (sieve-like) condition with respect to points.
(ii) 'Assez/presque dense', condition Sous-at 3': for every X ∈ M' there is x ∈ L ∩ F' with x ∘≪ X.
He notes that 3 ⇒ 3', and that each implies At 8 for F' and gives L' = L ∩ F'. He then observes that At 9 is not in general inherited by a sub-atelier, even a full one. To get it he imposes Sous-at 4: if X, Y ∈ M' and X ∥ Y in F, then X ∥ Y in F'. Here ∥ is a separation/incidence relation, so the relation is reflected by F'. The margin comment and the next page show the purpose: a bookkeeping check of which atelier axioms pass to sub-ateliers ('Énoncés 3, 4'). This is a routine stability analysis inside his own unpublished axiomatics of tame or combinatorial topology.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The claim 3 ⇒ 3' tacitly needs every X ∈ M' to have at least one interior point x ∘≪ X in L. That is presumably one of the atelier axioms (At 8), but it is not restated here.

ideas.what: Thick (point-saturated) sub-atelier: a figure in F' brings all its points from L into F'.
ideas.modern_name: Downward-closed / saturated subcomplex (sieve condition on the face poset)

ideas.what: Almost-dense sub-atelier: each distinguished figure of F' contains an interior point lying in F'.
ideas.modern_name: Density condition (roughly, existence of interior points in the subsystem)

ideas.what: Stability of the atelier axioms (At 8–14 bis) under passage to sub-ateliers, with an extra reflection condition Sous-at 4 for the relation ∥.
ideas.modern_name: Hereditary properties of axiomatic tame-topology structures (cf. o-minimal / stratified-space axiomatics)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; the 'atelier' framework itself is known only from these archive notes
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only sketches the programme of 'topologie modérée', without the atelier axioms

deep.surprise_reason: This is internal bookkeeping in Grothendieck's unpublished atelier axiomatics: definitions of thick and dense sub-ateliers, and checks of axiom inheritance. The framework as a whole is little known, but this page contains no notable result or connection.
transcription_corrections: 'Sous-cat (épais) 3' and 'Sous-cat (presque dense) 3'' should read 'Sous-at', i.e. sous-atelier.
In the definition, 'la sous-catégorie F' de F' should read 'le sous-atelier F' de F'.
'passage à une "sous-catégorie", même pleine' should read approximately 'passage à un "sous-atelier", même plein'.
'Pour être sûr d'en conclure, on rendra' is more likely 'Pour être sûr d'en conclure, on demande', introducing 'Sous-at 4'.
'Il est dit assez-dense': the image shows 'presque-dense'/'assez-dense' inserted above a crossed-out word.
The line 'et ces deux conditions impliquent At 8 pour F', et a fortiori impliquent directement L' = L ∩ F'' replaces the garbled 'l'intérieur indiquent directement'.
In the definition, '(pour les bornes)' is uncertain; it may be '(pour les points)'.
